column1: # Known-issue buckets for triage (fuzz.sh). One per line: ID<TAB>FIELD<TAB>ERE[<TAB>ERE]
#   FIELD: sig (the crash / differential signature), src (the input's text), or both
#   (the signature matches the first ERE and the input the second). A FIELD of sig-fixed /
#   src-fixed / both-fixed matches the same way but for a finding whose fix has already
#   landed: the pattern is often a loose bash-error substring that a genuinely NEW bug can
#   also produce, so a match is never silently bucketed -- it's printed under "regression
#   or variant of Fn (fixed)" for a human to check, instead of disappearing into the known
#   count (seen: F1-F15 fixed on main, a later triage still bucketed fresh diffs as
#   F2/F7/F8/F10 because their patterns are just bash's generic error wording).
# The first matching line names the bucket; nothing matching is reported as NEW.
# IDs are tools/fuzz/findings.md entries; UB/NOISE are not curse bugs (docs/bash-ub.md class,
# or nondeterminism the masks don't cover). Heuristic by nature: a NEW bucket that turns
# out to be a known bug gets a better line here.
# (fuzz-docker triage, F31-F52: before the older lines, whose *-fixed patterns are generic
# bash wording -- F2/F10 would otherwise claim F48/F49/F50 as "variants")
